Compiz should be able to do it, and since you said it's only happening on your secondary monitor it's going to be either a configuration issue we can sort out, or a GPU memory thing. (I know you posted your stats earlier, but it's my bedtime so just putting this out before I dip out)

Dig through manuals, guides, and configuration files for compiz and see if you can find anything about multi-monitor setup. Check your video driver config program as well (i.e. nvidia-settings), it may have what you need. Look for tags and options related to double- or triple-buffering, if you find this switched off for that monitor, you've got your fix.

Double- and triple-buffering is a process where the video card works ahead for the sake of smoother transitions between frames. If it's been turned off, or disabled for the specific monitor, you'll get tearing of the image when things are moving. I get it sometimes even when scrolling a heavily-detailed webpage, not just watching HD video.
